card.name: Words right before efficacy or effectiveness
card.fires_on: The word just before 'efficacy' or 'effectiveness', mostly 'and' after 'Safety' or 'safe', and the start of 'EFFICACY' in capitals. Also 'losing' before 'their effectiveness'.

modes.label: Safety and ...
modes.description: The word 'and' joining 'safety' or 'safe' to an expected 'efficacy/effective' in use-in-population statements.
modes.example: Pediatric Use Safety<< and>> effectiveness in pediatric patients under 12

modes.label: Start of EFFICACY
modes.description: The first piece of the capitalized word EFFICACY in a notice about color variation.
modes.example: YELLOW IS NORMAL AND DOES NOT ALTER<< EFF>>ICACY.

modes.label: Losing effectiveness
modes.description: A verb that leads straight into 'effectiveness' in storage advice.
modes.example: to prevent them from<< losing>> their effectiveness.

card.writes: It pushes the model to output 'effective', 'effectiveness' or 'efficacy' next.
card.plain: It fires when the text is about to say that a drug is effective or has efficacy, usually right after 'safety and'.
